originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons show June 2026 Fourier-ratio and October 22 energy papers lack the claimed finite support classification. The October 26 follow-up gives the 4|N coset branch, credited here, but poses the four-point classification as open in Question 9.1 and certifies only an N=17 local obstruction. published-finding corpus searches using indicator, Wiener norm, graph Fourier ratio, quotient-lift and progression aliases did not find a subsuming statement. The new result is the certified complete 8..128 equality classification for odd and twice-odd moduli, not an infinite conjecture or a claim of uniqueness by database search alone.

value.rationale: The case of four points is the first small cardinality left open by the exact known two- and three-point classifications; the 2026 follow-up explicitly requests the four-point equality families. A complete certified cutoff across 121 moduli detects all subgroup, antipodal quotient-lift and primitive progression regimes, excluding over ten million alternatives. The natural exact enumeration informs bipartite Fourier-ratio minimization and tests a mathematically motivated conjectural infinite classification, without claiming the latter or adding merely arbitrary unsupported invariants.
